recognize_zh: 視野中兩個顆粒性白血球：左上細胞整個細胞質被深紫黑色粗顆粒填滿，右下細胞核呈腎形至帶狀，黑色顆粒團偏聚在細胞一側；在碘造影劑注射後的血片中，這類黑色顆粒可出現在嗜中性球與較不成熟的骨髓系細胞。
features: Upper-left granulocyte with cytoplasm densely packed by coarse dark purple-black granules obscuring the nucleus
Lower-right granulocyte with an indented to band-shaped nucleus and a focal aggregate of dark granules
Pale pink cytoplasm with finer granules in the less involved cell
Background red cells with numerous echinocytes and scattered platelets
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows two granulocytes containing coarse, dark purple-black cytoplasmic granular material. In the upper-left cell the material densely fills the cytoplasm and obscures the nucleus, whereas the lower-right cell, with an indented to band-form nucleus, shows a focal aggregate of dark granules within otherwise pale granular cytoplasm. The red cells show numerous echinocytes. The densely granulated cell could be mistaken for a basophil; with the history of sampling after iodinated contrast and similar material in bands and immature granulocytes, findings are consistent with pigment in neutrophils and myeloid precursors.

ddx.vs: A basophil has uniformly sized purple-black granules and would not share the same granular clumps with adjacent bands and metamyelocytes.
Toxic granules are finer and diffusely distributed rather than coarse black aggregates.
Large dark granules are present in all granulocytes as an inherited trait, independent of contrast exposure or sepsis.
